title: e2e-latency-profiling-traces-2026-04-12
body:
Purpose:
Quick capture of end-to-end latency traces from the Apr 10-12 investigation. Focus is on p50/p95/p99 and per-stage breakdowns across the serving runtime for short- and medium-context requests. This is a working doc - notes, hypotheses and TODOs below.

Run summary:
- Run window: 2026-04-10 10:00-2026-04-12 17:00 PDT.
- Model variants: redwood-llama-7b (fp16), redwood-llama-7b-quant (4-bit), redwood-llama-13b (fp16) for comparison.
- Hardware: A100-80GB (dedicated pool), 32 vCPU routing nodes, NIC 25Gbps.
- Typical request shapes: short prompts (<=64 tokens output), medium prompts (~256 tokens), bursty arrival (Poisson with mean 120 rps).
- Key config: batching window=5ms, max batch=32, prefix KV cache enabled for repeated prefixes.

Overall E2E latency (per request; includes routing, batching, kernel, serialization):
- Short requests (<=64 tokens, redwood-llama-7b fp16): p50=82ms, p95=210ms, p99=470ms
- Medium requests (~256 tokens): p50=420ms, p95=1.1s, p99=2.6s
- Quantized variant (7b 4-bit) short requests: p50=95ms, p95=230ms, p99=520ms (slower tail due to occasional dequant steps)

Per-stage breakdown (median/p95/p99 for short requests, values in ms):
- Ingress & auth (routing node): p50=6 / p95=18 / p99=45  - mostly stable, occasional TLS handshake + auth DB latency.
- Request queuing (per-worker batching wait): p50=4 / p95=40 / p99=200 - p99 dominated by burst collisions and backlog during 2 short spike episodes.
- Prefix/KV lookup: p50=1 / p95=3 / p99=12 - cache hits negligible latency; misses fall through to model decode where KV build cost accounted.
- Model decode (token generation, includes kernel exec and KV cache management): p50=55 / p95=140 / p99=300 - main contributor to median and tail.
- Serialization & network egress (grpc/http + JSON): p50=10 / p95=12 / p99=25 - stable except when larger outputs are returned.
- Post-process (filters, safety checks): p50=6 / p95=8 / p99=18
- End-to-end observed client RTT matches aggregated sum within noise.

Trace observations / notable outliers:
- Two correlated spikes on 2026-04-11 at 11:12 and 11:18 (10-20s between events). Traces show long queuing (per-worker) combined with a spur of scheduling delays on the node (context switch count high). Related to cron job for nightly data sync that started unexpectedly (ops note: CRON-SYNC job SRV-1279).
- p99 tail often shows a mismatch: high queuing time followed by small model decode time - indicates a few requests waited for a large batch to form and then completed quickly. Suggests batching window settings create a long-tail under bursty traffic.
- Quantized model variant shows sporadic +30-70ms overhead on some traces where dequantization path triggers; likely due to mixed kernel fallback on that node. Traces correlate with a specific GPU driver version (470.114) on 2/8 hosts.
- Occasional auth DB latency spike adds ~40-60ms at p99 for a subset of requests originating from region eu-central-1.

Hypotheses:
1) Batching window at 5ms + max_batch=32 works well for steady traffic but under bursty arrival the batching wait creates heavy p99 tail because of backlog collisions.
2) Driver/kernel mismatch on small subset of dedicated GPUs causes dequant fallbacks and ~50ms penalty for quant models.
3) Background cron jobs on routing/worker machines can create CPU contention and long queuing delays; need stronger isolation and job scheduling guardrails.
4) Auth DB cross-region calls contribute to regional p99 - caching or local read-replicas could reduce this.

Immediate actions taken (during run):
- Rolled a small change to reduce batching window to 3ms for one canary pool (SRV-1287), re-ran traces - p95 reduced by ~12% for short requests, p99 reduced by ~8%.
- Marked two hosts with driver 470.114 for remediation. Patch PR opened: GITHUB:repo/PR#342.
- Added a guard to delay non-essential cron tasks during peak windows (ops ticket filed).

Data artifacts / where to find traces:
- Full trace replay: https://traces.internal.redwood/replay/2026-04-10/run-7
- Filtered p99 trace sample set: https://traces.internal.redwood/query?tag=p99-2026-04-11
- Raw perf logs (host metrics + perf): s3://perf-logs/serving-runtime/2026-04-10-to-12/

Next steps / TODOs:
- [ ] Finish root-cause on driver-related dequant fallbacks: reproduce on canary hardware, bisect kernel. Owner: Ethan. Due: 2026-04-18.
- [ ] Measure end-to-end impact of batching window changes under synthetic burst patterns (Poisson with mean 300 rps, alpha spikes). Owner: Maya. Due: 2026-04-16.
- [ ] Implement local auth read-replica for eu-central-1 and validate p99 improvements. Owner: Sofia. Due: 2026-04-22.
- [ ] Add trace-based alerting for sustained per-worker queue >100ms for >30s window (SLO guard). Owner: SRE. Due: 2026-04-20.
- [ ] Document recommended batch window templates per traffic profile in the Runbook (docs PR).

Notes / loose ideas:
- Consider adaptive batching: increase window briefly for very low QPS to improve throughput but cap tail impact. Could be per-customer profile.
- Investigate kernel-level preemption counters - if scheduling delays are due to long-running host-level tasks we can exile background jobs.
- For quant models, consider shipping a per-host diagnostic that records kernel fallback counts into metrics (so we can correlate without full trace replays).

Questions for review:
- Acceptable tradeoffs for p95 vs p99 when tuning batching window? (Product/Console team input requested)
- Is ops comfortable with driver rollout schedule to remediate the 2 hosts? (Ops/Infra)

References / related tickets:
- JIRA SRV-1287 (canary batching window change)
- JIRA SRV-1279 (cron sync causing spike)
- PR GITHUB:repo/PR#342 (driver remediation)
